title: Texas Stuns Ole Miss 34-27: 3 Key Takeaways from Burnt Orange Nation’s Upset Victory
body:
The Texas Longhorns edged past the Ole Miss Rebels 34‑27 on Saturday night, preserving their spot in the College Football Playoff bracket and keeping their national‑title aspirations alive. A hard‑fought victory that hinged on a late‑game surge and a clutch defensive stand, the win highlighted Texas’ resilience, underscored lingering offensive inconsistencies, and set the stage for a pivotal showdown with a top‑five opponent next week.

From the opening drive, Texas established a rhythm that seemed destined to carry them to an easy win. Quarterback Quinn Ewers orchestrated a balanced attack, mixing precise short passes with a handful of deep throws that resulted in two early touchdowns. The Longhorns built a 21‑10 lead by the midway point of the second quarter, prompting fans to believe the game was already decided. Yet Ole Miss, led by a revitalized offense under quarterback Jaxson Dart, refused to surrender. A series of quick strikes in the latter half of the second period narrowed the gap to three points, and a relentless ground game in the third quarter saw the Rebels claw back to within a single score.

The third quarter unfolded much like a déjà vu of earlier contests: Texas would surge ahead, only to watch Ole Miss answer back with equal vigor. Defensive lapses in the middle of the field allowed the Rebels to exploit mismatches, while Texas’ special teams struggled to contain return yards. Despite the back‑and‑forth, the Longhorns managed to stay ahead, largely thanks to a timely 45‑yard field goal by kicker Cam Bouldin and a crucial third‑down conversion that kept drives alive. However, the pattern of building a lead and then watching it evaporate raised questions about the Longhorns’ ability to close out games against elite competition.

The decisive moment arrived early in the fourth quarter when Texas’ defense forced a fumble deep in Ole Miss territory. Defensive end DeMarion Jones recovered the ball and returned it to the Rebels’ 22‑yard line, setting up a short touchdown run by running back Roschon Johnson. That play extended the lead to seven points and shifted momentum firmly back to Austin. Ole Miss answered with a quick touchdown pass, but a subsequent missed two‑point conversion left them trailing by five. With just under three minutes left, Texas executed a methodical drive, converting two critical third‑downs before Ewers found wide receiver Xavier Worthy for a 12‑yard touchdown that sealed the win.

Beyond the scoreboard, the game offered a clear lens into Texas’ strengths and vulnerabilities. On offense, the Longhorns demonstrated an ability to strike quickly and efficiently, particularly through the air, where Ewers posted a 12‑completion, 180‑yard performance. Yet the reliance on big plays also exposed a lack of sustained drives; the team managed only three possessions of over ten plays. Defensively, the unit showed flashes of dominance—particularly in the secondary, where cornerback Tyree Wilson recorded two interceptions—but also revealed susceptibility to play‑action passes that Ole Miss exploited throughout the second half.

Looking ahead, the Longhorns must address the inconsistency that plagued them against a resilient Ole Miss squad. Coaches will likely emphasize red‑zone efficiency and disciplined tackling to prevent the kind of momentum swings that nearly cost them the game. If Texas can tighten those edges, they stand a strong chance of advancing deeper into the playoff picture, especially with a high‑stakes clash against a top‑five opponent looming next week. For now, the victory serves as both a confidence boost and a reminder that the path to a national championship will demand flawless execution in the moments that matter most.
